passages.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, To the elect who are exiles of the Dispersion throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood: Grace and peace be yours in abundance.
passages.sermon:
Peter writes this letter.
Peter is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
He writes to God’s chosen people.
These people live as exiles.
They are scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
God the Father chose them long ago.
The Holy Spirit made them holy.
God chose them so they would obey Jesus Christ.
God chose them so they would be cleansed by the blood of Jesus Christ.
Peter prays that God will give them much grace.
Peter prays that God will give them much peace.
passages.original: Πέτρος ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἐκλεκτοῖς παρεπιδήμοις Διασπορᾶς Πόντου Γαλατίας Καππαδοκίας Ἀσίας καὶ Βιθυνίας κατὰ πρόγνωσιν Θεοῦ Πατρός ἐν ἁγιασμῷ Πνεύματος εἰς ὑπακοὴν καὶ ῥαντισμὸν αἵματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πληθυνθείη

passages.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! By His great mercy He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you, who through faith are shielded by God’s power for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last time.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God deserves blessing.
God has great mercy.
God gave us new birth.
God gave us new birth into a living hope.
God did this through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
God gave us an inheritance.
This inheritance cannot perish.
This inheritance cannot be defiled.
This inheritance cannot fade.
God keeps this inheritance in heaven for you.
God shields you by His power.
You receive this protection through faith.
God protects you for salvation.
This salvation is ready to be revealed.
God will reveal this salvation at the last time.
passages.original: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἀναγεννήσας ἡμᾶς εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν δι’ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐκ νεκρῶν εἰς κληρονομίαν ἄφθαρτον καὶ ἀμίαντον καὶ ἀμάραντον τετηρημένην ἐν οὐρανοῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς τοὺς ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ φρουρουμένους διὰ πίστεως εἰς σωτηρίαν ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι ἐν καιρῷ ἐσχάτῳ

passages.text: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials so that the proven character of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire—may result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
You rejoice in this hope.
Now, for a short time, you may have to suffer grief.
You face many kinds of trials.
These trials test your faith.
Your faith is more valuable than gold.
Gold can perish, even though it is refined by fire.
Your tested faith will be found genuine.
Your faith will result in praise.
Your faith will result in glory.
Your faith will result in honor.
This will happen when Jesus Christ is revealed.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε ὀλίγον ἄρτι εἰ δέον ἐστὶν λυπηθέντες ἐν ποικίλοις πειρασμοῖς ἵνα τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως πολυτιμότερον χρυσίου τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου διὰ πυρὸς δὲ δοκιμαζομένου εὑρεθῇ εἰς ἔπαινον καὶ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy, now that you are receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
passages.sermon:
You have not seen Jesus Christ.
You love Him.
You do not see Him now.
You believe in Him.
You rejoice in Him.
Your joy is inexpressible and glorious.
You are now receiving the goal of your faith.
This goal is the salvation of your souls.
passages.original: ὃν οὐκ ἰδόντες ἀγαπᾶτε εἰς ὃν ἄρτι μὴ ὁρῶντες πιστεύοντες δὲ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ κομιζόμενοι τὸ τέλος τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν σωτηρίαν ψυχῶν

passages.text: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who foretold the grace to come to you searched and investigated carefully, trying to determine the time and setting to which the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing when He predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories to follow.
passages.sermon:
The prophets spoke about the grace that would come to you.
These prophets searched carefully.
They investigated this salvation.
They wanted to know when and how these things would happen.
The Spirit of Christ was in them.
The Spirit showed them about Christ’s sufferings.
The Spirit also showed them about the glories that would come after Christ’s sufferings.
The prophets tried to find out the exact time and situation the Spirit meant.
passages.original: Περὶ ἧς σωτηρίας ἐξεζήτησαν καὶ ἐξηραύνησαν προφῆται οἱ περὶ τῆς εἰς ὑμᾶς χάριτος προφητεύσαντες ἐραυνῶντες εἰς τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρὸν ἐδήλου τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς Πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ προμαρτυρόμενον τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας

passages.text: It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves, but you, when they foretold the things now announced by those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.
passages.sermon:
God revealed something important to the prophets.
God showed the prophets that they were not serving themselves.
God showed the prophets that they were serving you.
The prophets foretold things about salvation and grace.
Now, others have announced these things to you.
These people preached the gospel to you.
They preached by the power of the Holy Spirit.
God sent the Holy Spirit from heaven.
Even angels desire to look into these things.
passages.original: οἷς ἀπεκαλύφθη ὅτι οὐχ ἑαυτοῖς ὑμῖν δὲ διηκόνουν αὐτά ἃ νῦν ἀνηγγέλη ὑμῖν διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμένων ὑμᾶς ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι

passages.text: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober-minded. Set your hope fully on the grace to be given you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Peter wrote this letter to Christians.
Peter told them to prepare their minds for action.
Peter told them to be sober-minded.
Peter told them to set their hope fully on the grace that will come to them.
This grace will be given at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Διὸ ἀναζωσάμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν νήφοντες τελείως ἐλπίσατε ἐπὶ τὴν φερομένην ὑμῖν χάριν ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: As obedient children, do not conform to the passions of your former ignorance.
passages.sermon:
You are children who obey God.
Do not shape your lives by your old desires.
You had these desires when you did not know God.
Do not follow those old passions now.
passages.original: ὡς τέκνα ὑπακοῆς μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς πρότερον ἐν τῇ ἀγνοίᾳ ὑμῶν ἐπιθυμίαις

passages.text: But just as He who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do, for it is written: “Be holy, because I am holy.”
passages.sermon:
God called you.
God is holy.
You must be holy in everything you do.
Scripture says, “Be holy, because I am holy.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸν καλέσαντα ὑμᾶς ἅγιον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἅγιοι ἐν πάσῃ ἀναστροφῇ γενήθητε διότι γέγραπται ὅτι Ἅγιοι ἔσεσθε ὅτι ἐγὼ ἅγιος εἰμι

passages.text: Since you call on a Father who judges each one’s work impartially, conduct yourselves in reverent fear during your stay as foreigners.
passages.sermon:
God is your Father.
God judges each person’s work.
God judges without showing favoritism.
You call on God as your Father.
You live as foreigners in this world.
Live with reverent fear during your time here.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰ Πατέρα ἐπικαλεῖσθε τὸν ἀπροσωπολήμπτως κρίνοντα κατὰ τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε

passages.text: For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life you inherited from your forefathers, but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot.
passages.sermon:
You know God redeemed you.
God did not redeem you with perishable things.
Silver and gold are perishable things.
You did not receive redemption through silver or gold.
You lived an empty way of life before.
You inherited this empty way of life from your forefathers.
God redeemed you from this empty way of life.
God redeemed you with the precious blood of Christ.
Christ is like a lamb without blemish or spot.
Christ’s blood is pure and valuable.
God used Christ’s blood to redeem you.
passages.original: εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ ἐλυτρώθητε ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ

passages.text: He was known before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in the last times for your sake.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the subject.
God knew Jesus Christ before He created the world.
God revealed Jesus Christ in the last times.
God revealed Jesus Christ for your sake.
passages.original: προεγνωσμένου μὲν πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου φανερωθέντος δὲ ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τῶν χρόνων δι’ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Through Him you believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and glorified Him; and so your faith and hope are in God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the one God raised from the dead.
God gave Jesus Christ glory.
You believe in God through Jesus Christ.
Your faith is in God.
Your hope is in God.
passages.original: τοὺς δι’ αὐτοῦ πιστοὺς εἰς Θεὸν τὸν ἐγείραντα αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόξαν αὐτῷ δόντα ὥστε τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν καὶ ἐλπίδα εἶναι εἰς Θεόν

passages.text: Since you have purified your souls by obedience to the truth so that you have a genuine love for your brothers, love one another deeply, from a pure heart.
passages.sermon:
You have purified your souls.
You did this by obeying the truth.
This led you to have a sincere love for your brothers and sisters.
Love one another deeply.
Love from a pure heart.
passages.original: Τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν ἡγνικότες ἐν τῇ ὑπακοῇ τῆς ἀληθείας εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας ἀλλήλους ἀγαπήσατε ἐκτενῶς

passages.text: For you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.
passages.sermon:
You have been born again.
God caused this new birth.
This new birth did not come from perishable seed.
This new birth came from imperishable seed.
The imperishable seed is the word of God.
God’s word is living.
God’s word endures forever.
passages.original: ἀναγεγεννημένοι οὐκ ἐκ σπορᾶς φθαρτῆς ἀλλὰ ἀφθάρτου διὰ λόγου ζῶντος Θεοῦ καὶ μένοντος

passages.text: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of the Lord stands forever.” And this is the word that was proclaimed to you.
passages.sermon:
All people are like grass.
All human glory is like flowers in a field.
Grass dries up.
Flowers fall.
The word of the Lord stands forever.
This word is the message that was preached to you.
passages.original: διότι Πᾶσα σὰρξ ὡς χόρτος καὶ πᾶσα δόξα αὐτῆς ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου ἐξηράνθη ὁ χόρτος καὶ τὸ ἄνθος ἐξέπεσεν τὸ δὲ ῥῆμα Κυρίου μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα Τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν εἰς ὑμᾶς
